rawFindings.title: Incorrect multiline detection in comma-dangle rule for 'always-multiline' option
rawFindings.explanation: The variable lastTokenOnNewLine was replaced by nodeIsMultiLine (checking if node location start and end lines differ). The later check correctly detects if the entire node is multiline, instead of only checking last token position relative to penultimate comma token. This is a correct behavior for determining if dangling comma is required or not.
rawFindings.suggestion: Retain new nodeIsMultiLine variable for multi-line detection as introduced in line 28 ensuring consistent multi-line checks.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect dangling comma detection logic for 'always-multiline' option
rawFindings.explanation: The original check used lastTokenOnNewLine flag comparing node end line to penultimate token end line, which is less reliable. The fix changes it to check nodeIsMultiLine (node start line !== node end line) for dangling comma validation which is logically correct for 'always-multiline'.
rawFindings.suggestion: Use nodeIsMultiLine for evaluating trailing comma presence/removal under 'always-multiline' option.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect missing trailing comma detection logic for 'always-multiline' option
rawFindings.explanation: Similarly, the missing comma detection switched from lastTokenOnNewLine to nodeIsMultiLine, aligning with the proper rule semantics that dangling comma is required if node spans multiple lines.
rawFindings.suggestion: Use nodeIsMultiLine for detecting missing dangling comma in 'always-multiline' mode.

rawFindings.title: Test cases updated to reflect corrected handling of multiline detection in 'always-multiline' option
rawFindings.explanation: Test cases previously expecting unexpected trailing comma or different positions adjusted to expect missing trailing comma at correct column positions consistent with the new nodeIsMultiLine logic.
rawFindings.suggestion: Update test code and error assertions to reflect corrected multiline trailing comma rule behavior.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect condition for multiline check in comma-dangle rule
rawFindings.explanation: The condition to determine if the node is multiline was incorrectly checking if the penultimate token and the node end are on different lines. The fix assigns a boolean `nodeIsMultiLine` to check if the node start and end lines differ and uses this for subsequent checks to correctly enforce 'always-multiline' option.
rawFindings.suggestion: Assign `var nodeIsMultiLine = node.loc.start.line !== node.loc.end.line;` at line 28 and replace checks `lastTokenOnNewLine` with `nodeIsMultiLine` in the following if statements at lines 42-45.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect multiline detection for trailing comma enforcement
rawFindings.explanation: The check for multiline objects or arrays for 'always-multiline' option was changed from comparing penultimate token end line and node end line to comparing node start line and end line. This is correct as the previous check incorrectly relied on token positions and could miss multiline nodes when penultimateToken and end token are on same line though node spans multiple lines.
rawFindings.suggestion: Keep the new variable nodeIsMultiLine defined as node.loc.start.line !== node.loc.end.line and use this boolean to decide if node is multiline instead of comparing penultimateToken.loc.end.line and node.loc.end.line.

rawFindings.title: Incorrect usage of nodeIsMultiLine in comma dangling logic
rawFindings.explanation: The condition for reporting errors when dangling comma is or is not present and the node is multiline was inverted in the patch. The previous logic used lastTokenOnNewLine (based on penultimateToken and node end line) which was changed to use nodeIsMultiLine correctly. This aligns with rulebehavior to require trailing commas only if the node spans multiple lines.
rawFindings.suggestion: Use nodeIsMultiLine as the determinant for reporting missing or unexpected trailing commas for the 'always-multiline' option as done in the patch.
